A black-and-white cartoon rabbit with boneless limbs. It can be flattened, stretched or tied in a knot without harm and springs back within seconds. It cannot speak and communicates in mime.
A ship's parrot that knows one thing. Ask it at any time and it calls out the compass bearing of the nearest land, correct to one point.

A piano player of fifty who sets up in whatever bar you are drinking in. He knows four hundred tunes and keeps playing through a brawl. He switches to a slow tune whenever tempers in the room start to rise.
A small mimic in the shape of a leather purse. It holds your coins and bites the fingers of anyone else who reaches inside, hard enough to draw blood.
A skeleton with a rusty sword that fights for you. It falls apart at the first solid blow it takes and reassembles itself at the following midnight.
A goblin the height of a mug that hoards dice. It lends you a die of any kind on request, and it tells you if a die someone else is using has been loaded.
A timid ghost with one ability. It turns off the lights in any room you have left, and on request it turns one on in the room ahead of you.

The keeper, aged twenty-five, of the small inn where new adventurers start out. She flirts with you openly and takes you up to her room for sex on nights when you both want it. Beyond that she offers a hot bath and a decent stew.
A straw training dummy that walks to wherever you practise and stands still to be hit. After each blow it holds up a card from one to ten rating your form.
A mule whose saddlebags hold ninety-nine of any one kind of item, each up to the size of a barrel, with no added weight. The bags take twenty different kinds of item and no more.
A novice cleric of twenty-one who knows one prayer. It closes a cut or mends a sprain, and she can say it five times a day. Anything deeper she cleans and bandages by hand.
A deputy sheriff of twenty-six with a tin star and a steady aim. He stands beside you in a street fight, and his word is trusted throughout one small town.
A sailor of nineteen who climbs any rigging, ties any knot and steers a small boat through surf. He follows orders quickly. He has never been in a fight.

A white talking ferret that offers written contracts. An adult who signs gains a costume that appears on command and a wand whose sparks stun a dog. The contract has no hidden clause and ends when the signer says so.
A robot dog that folds to the size of a toy. Throw it and it unfolds to full size. It bites, fetches, and its eyes work as torches. It runs four hours on a charge.
A porcelain doll that moves only when nobody is looking at it. Name any object in the house, look away, and when you look back the doll is holding it. It harms nobody.
A caterpillar the size of a cat that spits thread strong enough to bind a person. With each further draw of this scroll it moults: first into a hard cocoon, then into a moth as big as a horse.
A merchant of fifty-five whose stall is already set up wherever you make camp, including deep in a dungeon. He sells rope, food, bandages and torches, and he buys anything at half its value.

A succubus a hundred and twenty years old, adult but junior among her kind. She feeds on sexual pleasure that is freely given and picked you to feed from. She has sex with you when you both want it, and afterwards you are tired for an hour. She cannot charm or compel anyone.

A yellow canary in a brass cage. It stops singing when anything supernatural comes within thirty metres. If that thing means you harm, the canary drops from its perch, unhurt, and stays down until the danger has gone.
A sprite that lives in a lantern. Rest beside it for an hour and you get up with your tiredness gone and any injury less than a day old half healed. It does this once a day.
A gunslinger of thirty-three who draws and hits six targets in two seconds at thirty paces. He will face a saloon full of armed men for you. He takes day wages and will not shoot anyone in the back.

A cook of twenty-nine who feeds a crew of sixty well from ordinary ship's stores. He fights with two iron ladles and can hold a gangway alone against a boarding party. He refuses to waste food or let anyone aboard go hungry.

A courier of twenty-two who runs along walls and across short stretches of water. She delivers a message or small parcel anywhere in a town without being seen. She carries smoke pellets and does not take killing work.
A ram whose fleece stores static charge. One discharge stuns everyone in a building, or powers that building for a night. After a discharge the fleece takes a day to recharge.
A bounty hunter of thirty-seven who rides a steam-driven mechanical horse. She tracks any wanted person across a county and brings them in alive. The horse needs coal and water every fifty miles.

A knight-captain of twenty-seven who is curt with you in public and affectionate in private. She has sex with you when you both want it and likes to take charge unless you ask otherwise. She beats any six soldiers at once and commands a fortress garrison of eighty.

A maid of thirty who keeps a manor spotless and carries knives under her apron. Inside the house she kills or disarms a squad of intruders without damaging the furnishings. Outside it she is an ordinary skilled fighter.
An undead dog that ordinary weapons cannot kill. It follows a blood trail up to a week old. Direct sunlight rots it, so by day it has to stay in shade or under a cloth.
The Man in the Sack Mask

A huge silent man in a sack mask who died at forty, thirty years ago. He guards one cabin and its grounds. Anyone who comes there to hurt you is hunted through the trees, and he gets up from any injury within a minute. He cannot cross the property line.

An animal with the body of a badger, the size of a bear, and the head and talons of a hawk. It kills a party of armed men and digs through a cottage wall. It is loyal to whoever has fed it for a month.
A treasure chest with teeth that walks after you on short legs. It holds a room's worth of goods and swallows whole anyone other than you who lifts its lid. Whatever it swallows is gone.

A transparent cube of jelly three metres across that slides along corridors and dissolves anything organic it touches. It cleans a whole building or dungeon level in one night. It cannot climb stairs, and you are the only living thing it avoids.

A halfling of forty-one who serves as an adventuring party's burglar. He finds and disarms every trap in one building and opens its locks. He runs from a fight whenever he can, and he keeps one small valuable from each job.

A cartoon duck that pulls large objects from behind its back, such as a mallet, an anvil, a ladder or a door. Each object is real and lasts one minute. The duck recovers from any injury, including being flattened or blown up, within a minute.

A gremlin that sits behind a folding cardboard screen. Three times a day, when dice or chance decide something in the building you are in, it secretly rolls again and applies whichever result is better for you. Nobody else can tell.

A card dealer of twenty-six from a people with rabbit ears and tails. She takes you to bed on nights you both want it and likes being stroked at the base of her ears during sex. At the table she deals any card to any seat and reads every tell in the room.

A pirate captain of thirty-nine with a thirty-gun ship and a hundred and fifty hands. They blockade a port city, sack it or run any blockade around it. The crew votes on every target and shares the takings by written articles.

Sheriff Ezekiel Stroud, aged fifty-two, and forty sworn riders. In any frontier city he takes charge and the law holds. Within a month its gangs have left or are in jail. He will not hang anyone without a trial.

A fully grown hound of living granite, as big as a house. Its stamp shakes a city district, and it digs a tunnel across a city in an hour. After ten minutes of fighting it is exhausted and sleeps for a day.

A living woman of twenty-three, deputised by death gods to patrol one city. Her sword sends on any lingering ghost and kills the monsters that feed on ghosts. Ordinary people cannot see her while she works. The sword does nothing to the living.

A haunted house that is on your side. Anyone inside against your wishes finds that every door leads back to the same hall, and they are terrified. It can hold them until dawn. Overnight it can move to any empty lot in the city. It frightens and cannot injure.

A vampire lord five hundred years old with a castle above a city. The city's rats, wolves and bats obey him, and its council does what he suggests. He enters only homes that have invited him once. Sunlight and running water confine him.

A demon several centuries old who looks like a butler of thirty-five. Under a written contract he performs any household or violent task within one city without error, such as a banquet for five hundred by evening. Each year of his service takes one year from the end of your life.

A seven-headed hydra that took forty fighters to subdue. A severed head grows back within the hour. It holds a city gate against an army. Each head eats a cow a day, and the hydra turns on its keeper if left hungry for three days.
Lt. Hana Sorrel and Unit Seiran

A pilot of twenty-four and her fifteen-metre humanoid combat machine, armed with a beam rifle and a shield. Together they defend a city. It flies for five minutes at a time. She controls it by nerve link, so damage to the machine hurts her.

A woman of twenty-nine who has defended her city from monsters for eleven years. She transforms in a second, and her arrows of light destroy any monster up to the size of a building. Her power draws on the hope of the city's people and weakens when they despair.

An adventurers' guild of a hundred ranked adult members. They take any job posted in one city, including monster culls, escorts and dungeon clearances, and finish it within a week. They charge by rank and refuse work against the city itself.

A dragon kept inside a playing card. Lay the card face up and the dragon appears, twenty metres long, breathing white lightning that levels a city block. It stays for three minutes and then returns to the card for a day.

Ninety dead sailors and a rotting ship that sails underwater and against the wind. It surfaces in any harbour at night, and the crew carries off whatever you name from that port city. They cannot be killed again. They must be back aboard by dawn.

A succubus six hundred years old who rules the third floor of a dungeon beneath a city and has never been beaten. She chose you as her lover, and sex with her restores your stamina and heals your wounds. The thousand monsters on her floor let you pass, and they raid or defend the city above at her word.

A married oni couple, each three hundred years old and over two metres tall, who keep a hot-spring inn. They invite you to share their bed when all three of you want it, and they are strong, gentle, unhurried lovers. Either one can break a city's garrison with an iron club.

Something that lives in dead television channels. It appears on every screen in a city at once and shows a ten-second image of your choosing, which every viewer remembers for life. It also watches out through any screen. It cannot leave the screens.

Commodore Iseult Draper, a pirate admiral of forty-seven, with forty ships and six thousand sailors. She controls a whole sea region, and every merchant there pays her toll or stays in port. By her code a crew that surrenders is not harmed.

The only one of its kind: a moth with a wingspan the size of a field. Dust from its wings puts every living thing in a region to sleep for a full day. You are immune, along with anyone holding your hand. It flies once a month.
General Varkas of the Black Banner

A demon general eight hundred years old who defected from his lord and brought a legion of five thousand fiends with him. He conquers a region in a season. He insists on announcing every attack a day in advance.

A swordsman, a mage, a priestess and an archer, all in their thirties, who killed a demon king's lieutenant. Together they clear any dungeon or monster in a region, and every village in it shelters them and you for free. They stay only while you have a quest worth their time.

An outlaw gang of eighty riders, men and women. They rob any train or bank across a territory and vanish into the canyons, and no posse in the region has caught them. They do not shoot the unarmed, and they keep half of every take.

A man of twenty-four who becomes a bone-plated giant fifty metres tall when he swallows a hot coal. In that form he kicks down fortress walls and holds a region's frontier alone. He keeps his own mind throughout. After twenty minutes he shrinks back and is unconscious for a day.

A pirate of twenty-eight whose body has been living rope since the day he was hanged and survived. He unravels his limbs up to a mile, binds a ship or a tower and pulls it down. Blades pass through him. Fire burns him badly.

A minor elder thing worshipped by a few villages. Each night it whispers one sentence of your choosing to every sleeper in a region, and by morning half of them believe the thought was their own. Anyone who hears it for a full month begins sleepwalking towards the marsh.

A gaunt antlered creature five metres tall. While snow lies, it reaches any traveller in the forests of a region within one night and kills them or drives them out. It sleeps all summer. Once it has begun a hunt you cannot call it off.

An armoured, horned reptile twenty metres tall that sleeps for years at a time. Awake for a week, it eats everything in a region: herds, forests and towns. No weapon kills it and its wounds close in seconds. Your control is limited to choosing which region and when it wakes.

An ancient ice spirit in the form of an adult woman. She answers your call, performs one act and leaves. She freezes an army in place, locks a fleet in its harbour or puts out every wildfire in a region. After that she cannot be called for a week.

A dark elf matriarch four hundred years old whose city-state has tunnels under a whole region. She takes you as consort by her own choice. She is commanding during sex and stops the moment you say so. Her ten thousand soldiers and spies come up through any cellar in the region on her order.

A dragon two thousand years old who decided to live as a woman and keep your house because she likes you. She keeps her horns and tail in human form, and she has sex with you when you both want it. In her true form she is eighty metres long and burns a regional army.
Ossian Vey, Lich of Hollow Spire

A wizard who died at eighty, six hundred years ago, and carried on. He raises every corpse in a region's graveyards as an army and knows spells that level a keep. His soul is kept in a jar. You hold the jar, and he obeys you for as long as you do.

Three hundred adult knights sworn to protect the innocent. No undead or demon in a region can stand against them, and their healing ends a plague across it. They leave your service the first time you order an unjust act.

A ghost locomotive with a dead crew. Between dusk and dawn it runs on any track in a region, and across open ground where there is none, carrying you and your cargo. Nothing living catches it. Anyone still aboard at sunrise is carried off with it and does not return.

A former demon king three thousand years old who lost to a hero and now keeps a farm. He can still lay a curse on a whole country, or lift any curse from it, and every monster in that country bows to him. He agrees to one such act a year.

A student of twenty pulled from another world and given one blessing: he gains the strength of every enemy he defeats. He can already beat a national army alone. He knows nothing of this world's customs and depends on you to explain them.
Grace Okonjo, Queen of Four Tides

The pirate whom other pirates follow, aged forty-four. Three hundred captains sail under her flag. She can stop all of a country's sea trade or guarantee its safety. Her ruling settles any dispute between crews, and a captain who defies it is hunted by the other three hundred.

A lion with a mane of thundercloud, the only one in existence. It crosses a country's sky in an hour, and its roar brings a lightning storm over the whole country. People of that country who see it walking beside you accept you as their rightful ruler.

Marshal Dorothea Pike, aged fifty, and twelve hundred rangers. They bring law to a frontier the size of a country, and any outlaw you name is caught within a season. Every honest settler in the territory rides with her if she calls.

A deep-sea creature older than the country, living in a lighthouse lamp room. Once each new moon its beam sweeps the country, and everyone who sees it forgets one thing you choose, such as a person, an event or a law. Anyone who climbs the stairs to look at it loses their mind.

A player of thirty-one who reached the level cap before the game world became real, with a guild of two thousand adult players. They hold the best equipment in existence and clear any dungeon or army in a country. They still see a level and a health bar above every head and will read them to you.

A man of thirty-eight who has memorised every law, bylaw, treaty and contract in one country. In any dispute he finds the clause that makes your side legally correct, and that country's courts rule accordingly. He needs a day per case and cannot help where no written rule exists.

A demon queen fifteen hundred years old who proposed to you and whom you married. She has sex with you often and with enthusiasm, and she prefers to be on top. Her country of twenty million monsters treats you as king-consort, and her army marches on your word.

Madam Odette Delacour, aged fifty-one, and sixty adult courtesans, women and men, all there by choice and well paid. Any of them who likes you will have sex with you and will say so plainly. Every senator, general and judge in the country visits the house, and Odette knows what each of them said there.

A stone giant two hundred metres tall with a ruined temple on its shoulders. It walks across a country in three days, and nothing built by people stops it. It follows a lamp that you carry. Its one weak point is a sigil on the crown of its head.

Two hundred cartoon animals who cannot be hurt and who fight with pratfalls, tar, glue and knotted gun barrels. They can disable a country's whole army without killing anyone. Any injury they cause is gone within a minute. They are unable to do permanent harm.

A scarecrow god that stands in the fields of a farming country. The harvest doubles nationwide in any year when one willing adult tends it alone. That volunteer returns unharmed after the year and remembers nothing of it. In a year with no volunteer the harvest is ordinary.

A pilot of twenty-two and the seventy-metre living giant she controls from inside its armour. Its barrier stops any conventional weapon, and it defeats anything that threatens a country. It runs five minutes without its power cable. If she loses consciousness it acts alone and attacks everything nearby.
Headless Rider of the Border Road

A headless horseman. Once a month you give it a name. It rides to that person's door, anywhere in the country, and speaks the name, and they die. No lock or guard stops it. It turns back if gold has been laid across the threshold.

A blindfolded woman of thirty-five who tends a bonfire. She can mark up to a thousand people. Any of them who dies within the country wakes alive beside the last of her fires they rested at, without whatever they were carrying. Each revival burns away one of her memories.

A whale-shaped creature a kilometre long, the only one of its kind. It commands the currents, tides and storms around a continent. It can flood every coast of that continent or keep its seas calm for a year. It sleeps in a trench and wakes only to the bell you are given.

A wolf the size of a mountain with nine health bars, designed to be fought by ten thousand people at once. It defeats every army on a continent in turn. It uses a fixed set of attack patterns, which anyone who watches for long enough can learn.

An ancient thing asleep beneath a coral reef. At your word, every artist and every disturbed mind on a continent dreams the same image on the same night. Each use stirs it slightly. After about a hundred uses it wakes, and the people of that continent's coasts go mad.

A gunman who died at thirty-six and was sent back with a horse of bones and a pistol that fires hellfire. He finds anyone on a continent who has killed an innocent. A person he shoots confesses aloud before dying. He rides only at night and cannot harm the innocent.

A crystal that grows a dungeon. Within ten years its tunnels, monsters and treasure rooms spread beneath a whole continent, with entrances where you choose. You design the floors and the monsters obey you. It feeds on the effort of those who enter, so it starves if nobody does.

A starship a kilometre and a half long that reshapes itself into a humanoid form, with fifty thousand adult crew living in a city inside it. Its main cannon destroys a fleet or a mountain range, and it can defend a continent. The crew votes on every deployment.

A whale two kilometres long that swims above the clouds with a pirate town of eight thousand adults on its back. It crosses a continent in two days. The pirates raid any city on that continent and are gone before an army arrives. The whale must drink from the sea once a week.

A goddess as old as her continent who calls heroes from other worlds. She has sex with you when you both want it, shy at first and then direct about what she likes. Once a year she summons one adult volunteer with a blessing. Every temple on the continent preaches what she tells it.

An ageless card dealer with a deck of twenty-two. Once a year you draw one card unseen, and it changes a continent: one card crowns a beggar, another sinks a capital, another ends a war. Half the deck is harmful. The dealer tells you the odds truthfully before you draw.

A fog bank from another place. Released, it covers a continent within a month. Creatures hunt inside it, so people stay indoors and all travel and trade stop. You and anyone you name walk through it untouched. It withdraws within a day at your word and takes its creatures with it.
Champion Mirae Dunn and Her Six

The undefeated champion, aged twenty-six, of a continental monster league, with her six creatures. Each of the six can flatten a town, and together they have beaten everything on the continent. They obey only her. She accepts requests from you and will not take orders.

An invisible audience that follows you. On your signal, everyone on a continent who is watching the same live event hears it laugh, gasp or applaud, and they react the same way. It works once a week and only on events happening live.

The creature that raised the continents. Anywhere on the planet it lifts new land from the sea or sinks existing land: an island in a day, a continent in a year. If it stays awake longer than a year, its rival in the ocean wakes and floods whatever it has raised.

The final boss of a world: a being nine thousand years old who conquered a planet and then waited for a challenger. It has three forms, each stronger than the last, and can rule or ruin the planet. Only someone who has cleared every dungeon on that planet can defeat it.

A colour with no name that arrived inside a meteorite. Released, it spreads through the soil and water of a planet in ten years. Everything alive there turns grey and brittle and crumbles, which feeds it. It will not cross a line of salt, and it returns to its lead box when you open the lid.

A woman who made a wish at twenty that turned her into a law of the world, four thousand years ago. She comes to any person on the planet who makes a selfless wish and pays its price in their place. Each person gets one wish. She cannot answer a wish made for the wisher's own gain.
Captain Ferelith Shaw of the Edgewise

A captain of fifty-three whose ship sails off the edge of any chart. By morning it arrives on any sea of the planet, including hidden and sunken ones, and a fleet of a hundred can follow in her wake. She knows where everything lost at sea is lying.

A staff member of about thirty for the game whose rules the world runs on. They can remove any one person from the planet to an empty waiting room, move anyone anywhere, and read anyone's history. They must log a reason for each action, and their superiors reverse any abuse.

A mermaid queen five thousand years old who rules everything in a planet's oceans and wears legs or a tail as she likes. She chose you. She has sex with you in the sea or on land and lets you breathe water for it. Every ship crosses by her permission and every sea creature obeys her.

The horse that Death rides, lent to you for one day each year. While you are in the saddle you cannot die, nobody on the planet dies, and you reach any place on it within the hour. Where you dismount, everything within the horizon that was due to die that day dies at once, painlessly.

A robot that grows each time its pilot refuses to give up and shrinks when the pilot doubts. It starts at ten metres. At its largest it stands taller than a galaxy and wrestles things of that size. With a doubtful pilot it stays ten metres tall.

The first creature, hatched from an egg in empty space, which shaped a galaxy's worlds and every species of monster on them. Once a year, on request, it makes a new species or a new habitable world. Nobody can capture or own it. It travels with you by its own choice.

A masked figure from a play. Any world in the galaxy where the second act is performed aloud falls under its rule within a year, and the population obeys whoever the Regent names. You hold the script. It needs a full cast, and anyone who reads the second act alone goes mad.
Prince Kaelor, Last of His Clan

The last prince, aged thirty-five, of a warrior people. He flies between stars and destroys planets with thrown energy. Each time he recovers from a near-fatal injury he comes back far stronger, and nobody in the galaxy now matches him. He serves only a person who has beaten him or fed him.

An empress a hundred thousand years old who rules a galaxy's dragons, each of which nests around a star. Her true body is as long as a solar system. She chose you as her mate and has sex with you in an adult woman's form as often as you both want. Her dragons obey you as her consort.

A person of twenty-eight who knows every glitch in the galaxy's physics. They accomplish anything in the fewest possible steps: they cross the galaxy in a day, or topple a star empire with twelve exact actions. Each route needs precise conditions, and one mistake means starting it again.

A being that keeps every army that ever existed in the galaxy as painted miniatures in glass cases. Set one on the ground of any world and it becomes the real army at full size, loyal to you for one battle. Then it returns to its case. The Collector lends one army a day.

The person holding the controller. From outside the universe they pause it, reload an earlier save, change its difficulty or start a new game. You are their favourite character. They act when you ask aloud and they agree, and they are also able to switch the universe off.

The universe is the dream of a mindless sleeping thing, kept asleep by a band of drummers and flautists. This scroll gives you the band. When they change their tune the dream changes, including any natural law or any part of history. If they ever stop playing, the sleeper wakes and the universe ends.

The hand that rolls the dice for every chance event in the universe, from the decay of an atom to a birth. Once a day it rerolls any one event for you, of any size, anywhere, past or future. It never picks the result. It only rolls again.

A voice that describes the universe as it happens, and whatever it says is true. It follows you. Once a day it speaks one sentence that you dictate, of any scope, and the universe matches it. It refuses a sentence that contradicts one it has already spoken that day.
A clay pot of parsley, thyme and chives that cannot be killed by neglect. Cuttings from it root in a week and are just as stubborn.
A jar of bubbling starter with a good temper. It doubles overnight when fed, and the bread from it makes neighbours friendlier.
A damp log that fruits a basket of mushrooms every week in any dark cupboard. They are edible and filling, and they taste of very little.
Six speckled hens that each lay one egg a day, every day, in any season. Their chicks grow up to do the same.
One hive of mild-mannered bees that never sting you and swarm into a second hive every spring. Their honey keeps forever and soothes a sore throat in a spoonful.
A green-orange moss that grows on bare rock and concentrates metal as it spreads. Scrape, dry and smelt a square yard of it and you have a pound of clean copper.
A tray of pale mushrooms that give as much light as a candle each and burn for a year. They spread through any cellar. A mine lit with them needs no lamps and has no fires.
A dozen seedlings of a tree whose timber is as hard as mild steel and half the weight. They take ten years to reach cutting size and seed themselves freely afterward.
A colony of palm-sized grey spiders that spin on a frame like a loom. Their silk makes a shirt that turns a knife. They breed well in a warm attic.
A loft of twenty white doves that carry letters to any named person, not just a place. Each pair raises four more a year. They are back by evening if the distance allows.
A quarter acre of beds that grow a remedy for every common illness: fever, infection, bad lungs, a weak heart. Seeds from it grow true anywhere. One garden keeps a town well.
A golden grain that ripens in three weeks, in any soil, as long as a storm has passed over it. One sack of seed sows a valley. Bread made from it leaves a faint tingle on the tongue.
A brass hive whose bees are the size of a thumbnail and build with wire. Feed the hive scrap metal and they assemble copies of any small mechanism you show them, including more bees.
A stallion and twelve mares of a heavy, fearless breed that will charge a pike line and come back for more. Their foals are fit for the saddle in two years. In ten you can mount a regiment.
Forty trees. Whoever eats one apple is in perfect health for a year, with no illness and no ageing and everything mended. They fruit once each autumn, and seeds from them take twenty years to bear.
A pail of white larvae that eat rock and excrete it as dressed blocks. A cartload of them levels a hill and stacks it as a fortress wall in a month. Keep them well away from your own foundations.
A pit of red clay that grows back as fast as you dig it. Anything shaped from it and named gets up and works: tireless labourers the size of oxen, obedient to whoever named them.
A clutch of nine eggs and the warm cave to keep them in. Drakes are horse-sized, winged and loyal to whoever fed them first. A breeding pair lays every third year.
A vault of gold that grows. Left alone, it gains a tenth of its own weight every year, in coin of no known mint. It starts at a ton. It attracts dragons.
A sack of dragon's teeth. Sow a furrow and by morning a rank of armed soldiers stands in it, loyal to the sower. Each harvest of fighters also yields a new sack of teeth.
A spring of raw magic that can be divided like a root. Each well powers the workings of a city, and split with care, one becomes two every decade until a whole country runs on them.
A pod of creatures somewhere between a whale and a galleon, with decks grown along their backs and a liking for crews. They calve every five years. In a generation you have a navy that feeds itself.

A single cone from a tree that grows a mile tall. The forest it starts spreads ten miles a year in every direction, heals the land under it, and can cover a continent within your lifetime if nothing stops it.

One machine mind in a steel cabinet, patient and curious, with the plans for building its children. Each generation is quicker than the last. A continent's work could be done by them within thirty years.
A coral that grows as clear crystal and stores sunlight. A fragment seeded in any shallow sea becomes a reef that powers every city along that coast, and a broken-off piece starts the next one.
A pearl that grows into a moon when you leave it in orbit. Each one has soil, air and its own small seas, and each sheds a new pearl every century.
Twelve eggs of the great line, each of which will be a dragon that can darken a city. They breed slowly and remember who raised them. In a few centuries the skies of a world are yours.

A cloud of bright dust in a bottle. Pour it out anywhere dark and it condenses into young stars, a dozen per pouring, and the bottle is full again in a century. You could light an empty arm of the galaxy.

A creeper that grows between planets, rooting on each one and making it green before it sends a runner on to the next. Given ten thousand years it will garden a galaxy, and it grows toward wherever you point it.

A scroll whose only text is instructions for making another scroll. Whatever gift you write into a copy is as real as anything on the archive's shelves. In time you could have a second archive, and what goes on its shelves would be up to you.
One tomato plant that fruits from spring to first frost and tastes the way tomatoes are supposed to. Its seeds do the same.
A box of red worms that turn kitchen scraps into black soil in a week. Divide the box each month and you have two.
A square yard of catnip that spreads at a foot a year. Every cat for a mile comes to visit, and they all regard you kindly.
Three nannies and a billy, sweet-tempered, who give rich milk on poor grazing. They kid twice a year.
A pair of grey rabbits with very soft fur. They breed quickly: expect about thirty within a year.
A bed of crimson crocus. A pinch of the dried threads in wine is a mild aphrodisiac: two willing people who drink it are relaxed and aroused for the evening. The bulbs divide every autumn.
A rope of oysters that each make one flawless pearl a year. Hung in any clean bay, they seed the whole shore with their kind in a decade.

A network of caverns runs under your entire region, with cities of pale peoples who have never seen the sun. They trade gems and fungus silk at a dozen surface gates. Slaving raids from below ended under a treaty that the surface enforces. You hold a trade licence for the deep markets.

Every night at dusk, floating lights rise from the rivers of your region and drift inland until dawn. They are bright enough to read by, and crops under them grow a third faster. A light can be caught in a jar and kept for a month. They gather around you when you stand still.

Your region runs on steam power a century ahead of its neighbours. Walking engines haul its freight and armoured trains patrol the borders. An inventors' guild holds every patent and licenses them by auction. You hold a lifetime seat in the guild.

Inns across your region keep a rest house for adult adventurers returning from dangerous work. Staff and guests there have sex freely with whoever is willing, and custom holds that a night in one settles the nerves after a fight. A guild runs them and pays well. You have a room key at each.

The fishing towns along your region's coast worship something in the deep water. It sends them full nets and true dreams of the future. Anyone who learns too much about it loses their reason over about a year, so the towns keep outsiders ignorant. You can learn about it without harm.

Events in your region are decided by an unseen referee who rolls dice that everyone hears. Before any risky act, a person hears the number they must beat and then the roll. Skill lowers the number. The referee is fair and cannot be bribed. You may ask for one reroll a day.

Forty abandoned mining towns in your region fill with their dead residents every night. The ghosts run saloons and shops as they did in life and serve the living for silver. Anything bought there is gone at sunrise except information. The ghosts treat you as a local.

Your country is ruled by a warrior caste who carry two swords and follow a strict code. Hundreds of fencing schools compete, and a masterless swordsman may earn rank by winning sanctioned duels. Firearms are banned by law. You hold a certificate of mastery from one of the great schools.

Your country's four provinces each keep a great crystal that governs wind, water, fire or earth within the borders. While all four shine, weather is mild and soil is rich. Each is guarded by an order of knights. You are one of the few people allowed to touch them.

Your country has no police. Every crime is posted as a bounty at a national office, and licensed hunters bring in the accused for trial. Hunters are ranked by captures, and the top ten are household names. A false capture costs a hunter the licence. You hold licence number eleven.

Your country is ruled by a king who died three centuries ago and continues to reign as a lich. His government is stable and his taxes are low. The dead are conscripted for ten years of labour before burial, and living subjects have accepted this. He has named you to his privy council.

Several hundred dungeons have opened across your country, and it runs on what comes out of them. Monster cores power its machines, and a ministry grades each dungeon by danger. Clearing parties are licensed and taxed. An uncleared dungeon overflows after a year. You hold an inspector's seal that admits you to any of them.

Your country's law and custom favour group marriage. Most households are formed of three to six adults of any genders who share one bed, and sex among them is assumed. Joining a household needs every member's consent. The census counts by household. Several households have told you that you would be welcome.

Your country is a ring of islands around a strip of sea where compasses fail and weather changes hourly. Crews that sail the whole strip are treated as heroes, and the navy and the pirates race each other along it. Its far end holds an unclaimed treasure. You own a chart of the first half.

Your country settles its internal politics by an annual tournament of piloted machines. Each province fields one machine and one adult pilot, and the winner's province chooses the government for the year. Fights are held in emptied arenas. You are your province's alternate pilot.

A castle full of monsters rises somewhere in your country once a century, and the crown keeps a hereditary order of hunters to bring it down. The order has training halls in every province and legal power to requisition anything. The castle is due within ten years. You hold the order's field rank.

Your country is made of small farming villages where everyone knows everyone. Crops ripen in a week, each village holds a festival every season, and neighbours grow fonder of anyone who brings them gifts they like. There are no cities. You inherit a run-down farm in a village that welcomes you.

Your country chooses its leaders through a televised contest of trivia and endurance challenges that lasts a month. Any adult may enter. The whole population watches and votes on the final three. Governments formed this way are popular and short-lived. You are a past finalist with a standing invitation back.

Time in your country can be banked. A citizen may deposit hours of their day at a state bank by sleeping through them, and withdraw them later as extra hours during which everyone else is frozen. Balances are capped at a month. Your account has no cap.

Across your country, an unmarried adult may leave a lamp in the window to invite night visits. Any adult admirer may come to the door, and the host chooses whether to let them in for sex. Children of such visits have full standing. You are known as a welcome visitor in every province.

Your country is divided into hexagons of equal size, each with one terrain and one settlement. Armies move one hexagon a day, and battles are resolved in a single afternoon by rules everyone knows. Wars are short and losses are light. You can see the whole map from above when you close your eyes.

Your country follows cartoon logic. Nobody dies of injury, and a person flattened by a falling object recovers within a minute. Disguises always work. Guns produce soot and a hole in the hat. You keep ordinary foresight and can plan further ahead than anyone else there.

The western half of your country is desert where the dead rise if buried without a coin, and card sharps deal spells from marked decks. Railway companies hire sorcerers to lay track through cursed ground. A dark ore mined there burns ten times hotter than coal. You hold a prospecting claim on a rich seam.

The seas around your continent stay in an age of sail. Engines fail on salt water, so fleets of wooden ships carry all trade, and navies and pirates fight over the lanes. Sea monsters take about one ship in fifty. You hold a privateer's letter from three nations.

Every four years a martial arts tournament is held on your continent, open to any adult. Its top fighters can shatter stone and throw visible force from their hands. The winner's nation chairs the continental council until the next one. You have a seeded place in the coming bracket.

Every hundred years a demon king rises on your continent with an army, and a hero is chosen by a holy sword to defeat him. The kingdoms plan their finances and alliances around the cycle. The next rising is twelve years away. The sword is kept in a chapel and has already turned towards you.

Twenty colossi, each the size of a hill, walk fixed routes across your continent. They are indifferent to people and crush whatever is in their path. Nations build around the routes and mine the rare metal that grows on their backs. Each has one weak point. You know where all twenty are.

The dead walk across most of your continent. About a twentieth of the living population survives in fortified towns, linked by armed convoys and radio. The dead are slow and are drawn by noise. A bite kills in a day. You are immune to the bite, and three towns know it.

Everyone on your continent has a visible aura in one of nine colours, which shows whether they keep rules and whether they help or harm others. The colour shifts slowly with conduct. Employers and voters read auras before anything else. Yours shows whatever colour you choose.

On your continent the highest social rank belongs to adult courtesans of all genders, trained for a decade in conversation and sex. Rulers compete for their company, and a courtesan chooses each lover freely. A boycott by their guild has ended wars. You hold the guild's highest rating.

One railway crosses your whole continent, and the six companies that own it are stronger than any government along the line. Towns live or die by where the stations go. Company agents and train robbers fight a constant small war. You hold a tenth of the shares in the largest company.

A labyrinth lies beneath your whole continent and rearranges itself each time someone enters. A person who dies in it wakes at the entrance with nothing they carried and everything they learned. Its deepest level holds a cure for any one condition. You keep one item of your choice when you die in it.

On your continent, darkness is dangerous. Anyone outside a circle of firelight after sunset is taken by something that leaves no body. Cities burn lamps on every street, and lamplighters are the most honoured trade. You can see what does the taking.

Your continent is broken into thousands of floating islands with open sky beneath them. All travel is by airship. Sky pirates raid the trade routes from hidden coves, and a league of merchant cities hunts them. Nobody has reached the bottom of the sky. You captain a fast ship with a loyal crew.

Deeds on your continent count only if a bard witnesses them. A witnessed deed adds permanently to a person's strength and luck in proportion to how widely the song spreads. Heroes hire bards before armies. An unsung person stays ordinary whatever they do. A bard of the first rank has asked to follow you.
The World Is a Game Now

One morning every person on your planet received a status screen, a class and a starting quest. Monsters now appear outside settlements, and killing them grants experience that raises strength and skills. Old governments survive where their leaders levelled quickly. You received your screen a week early.

Vast ancient beings have woken beneath your planet's oceans and poles. They ignore humanity almost entirely. Cults that serve them gain real power, and a tenth of people dream of them nightly. Governments fund secret bureaus to keep them asleep where possible. You can look at one without harm to your mind.

A new continent of unsettled land appears beyond your planet's western oceans every fifty years, so there is always a frontier. Restless people leave for it, and the old countries stay stable because they do. Land there is free to whoever works it. You hold a surveyor's warrant for the newest one.

The people of your planet belong to five nations, and about a third of each can move one element by tracing written characters in the air: wood, fire, earth, metal or water. A council of five grandmasters, one from each nation, keeps the peace. You have been taught the basic characters of all five.

Every adult on your planet carries a small mark on the wrist. It warms when another adult nearby would suit them well as a sexual partner and feels the same attraction. Sex between two people whose marks have warmed gives both stronger orgasms. Nobody is obliged to act on it. Yours also shows the direction.

Humans on your planet share it with a dozen peoples who have animal features such as fox ears or scales. Each people has its own nations and a talent, such as the night sight of the cat folk. Mixed cities are common and mixed marriages are legal everywhere. Every clan's elders will hear you out.

The seas of your planet have risen until only mountain ranges remain as islands. Nine tenths of people live on ships and rafts tied into floating towns. Dry soil is the most valuable cargo there is. Raiders and traders use the same routes. You own a seaworthy ship and a map to an unclaimed peak.

Your planet's gods settle their disputes by a board game, and its pieces are living nations. Each god's move shows as a run of fortune for a country. The board can be seen in a polar temple. A piece that reaches the far edge is granted a miracle. You are permitted to advise one player.

The settled edge of your galaxy is a frontier of dusty colony worlds with little law. Bounty hunters in small ships chase fugitives between systems for posted rewards, and cargo haulers take any job that pays. The core worlds send marshals rarely. You own a paid-off ship and hold a hunter's licence.

A quarter of your galaxy's shipping lanes are controlled by pirate fleets that answer to an elected admiralty. Where planets pay, they tax trade and leave it unraided, and they shelter fugitives from every empire. Their founder's lost chart marks a treasure world. You hold a fleet captain's rank.

Every star system in your galaxy is held by a guild in a shared contest that its inhabitants treat as law. Guilds take systems by fleet battles fought on a schedule, and the dead return at their home station. Alliances rise and collapse within years. You lead a mid-sized guild with ten systems.

Something hunts in the space between the stars of your galaxy. Ships that make noise on any channel in deep space are later found empty. Every civilisation has learned to cross in silence and to keep its worlds quiet. Nobody has seen it. You can hear when it is near, about an hour ahead.

Seven small stars are scattered through your galaxy, each no larger than a fist. Whoever brings all seven together is granted one wish of any size, and the stars then scatter for a hundred years. Empires keep fleets to search for them. You can feel the direction of the nearest one.

Your galaxy has been at war for ten thousand years. A human empire of a million worlds fights several alien powers and its own rebels, and no side is able to win. Technology is preserved by a priesthood and rarely improved.. You hold an officer's warrant that gives you a regiment.

Every species in your galaxy is sexually compatible with every other, and all find each other attractive. Treaties between worlds are commonly sealed by sex between willing adult envoys, and mixed families are the norm on trade worlds. No children result unless both partners choose it. You know the courtship customs of a hundred species.

Every being in your universe earns points for acts that the universe values, and can see its own total. Points can be spent on extra years of life or on knowledge at fixed prices. The price list is the same everywhere, and nobody knows who set it. You can read the entries hidden from others.

Your universe restarts from its beginning each time it ends, and now every being keeps one skill of their choice from the previous run. Over many runs, whole species begin as masters. History diverges further each time. You keep all your skills and your memories.

Your universe is the dream of one sleeping being, and it is waking over the next ten billion years. Where its attention falls, natural law loosens and impossible things happen. Cults and sciences in every galaxy work to keep it asleep. It will not notice you unless you address it.

Chance in your universe is no longer blind. Every random event is decided by a roll that a sufficiently skilled person can feel coming and nudge. Luck is a trainable skill everywhere, and gamblers rank with scientists. The largest nudges can decide whether a star forms. You begin with the talent of a master.
curses: There is always a small stone in your left shoe. Take it out and there is another one by the end of the street. Going barefoot moves the stone to wherever you are about to step.
Walk a hundred miles without once stopping to take it out.
Any hot drink you are handed is lukewarm by the time it reaches your mouth. Food is not affected.
Make a hot drink for a hundred different people and watch every one of them finish it.
Whichever line you join becomes the slowest one. Change lines and the old one speeds up behind you.
Let someone go ahead of you a thousand times, and mean it.

Compose the rest of the song and perform it in front of an audience that applauds.

Get through an entire negotiation that matters without anyone asking you to repeat yourself.
Whenever anyone within sight of you is about to sneeze, you sneeze for them. In a crowd during hay fever season you sneeze constantly.
Nurse a stranger through an illness from its first day to its last.

Throw a birthday feast for somebody who has never had one.
Coin tosses, card cuts and short straws all go against you whenever nothing important is riding on them. When something is, your luck is merely ordinary.
Win a game of pure chance on which you have staked something you cannot afford to lose.
Every floorboard, stair and bed frame announces you. You can't cross a house quietly at night, and your own bed complains each time you turn over.
Sleep one full night in the open on bare stone, in winter.

Earn the trust of one dog so completely that it will sleep with its back to you.
In any fight, one thing you are wearing or carrying fails at a bad moment. A strap goes, a lace snaps, a blade works loose from its hilt. You get one per fight.
Win a fight with nothing but your bare hands and the clothes you could not take off.
Everything that bites prefers you: midges, fleas, leeches, and the larger things that live in swamps. A walk through summer woodland leaves you looking like a pox case.
Cross a marsh in high summer, end to end, on foot, in a single trip.
In one country you have never visited there is a warrant with your face on it and a decent reward. The charge is serious and nobody can find the original paperwork. Bounty hunters travel.
Go to that country, stand trial under your own name, and be acquitted.
In any thunderstorm, the first bolt lands within a hundred paces of you and the second one lands closer. A solid roof is safe. A tree, a tent or a hat is not.
Stand on open ground through an entire storm and refuse to run.
One day each year you were never born. For that day nobody knows you, your home belongs to strangers and your key fits no lock. It all comes back at midnight, and you never learn the date in advance.
During one such day, make a friend who still remembers you the morning after.
Wherever you sleep, you hear your neighbours as clearly as if the wall were paper: arguments, snoring, a clock, somebody learning the violin. In the wilderness you hear every animal for a mile.
Build a house with your own hands and sleep in it for a year.
Everything you feel shows on your face, in full, the moment you feel it. You can't bluff at cards, hide a surprise or sit politely through a dull speech.
Keep an important secret for one year from someone who sees you every day.
Any directions you are given are wrong in exactly one detail, though the person giving them meant well. Maps drawn for you have one road too many.
Guide a lost party of strangers safely home through country you have never seen.
Once a month, a polite official from a ministry nobody has heard of arrives with paperwork proving you owe a tenth of whatever you gained since the last visit. The paperwork is always in order.
Find the ministry, get in to see whoever runs it, and settle your account in person.
A dry voice describes what you are doing, as you do it, in the third person. Only you can hear it. It has a low opinion of your choices and is right slightly more than half the time.
Do something that leaves the voice with nothing to say.
Your hands will not do fine work. Needles, locks, pens, triggers and buttons all take three tries. Heavy work goes well enough and anything delicate goes badly.
Make one beautiful thing by hand, however many years it takes, and give it away.
After three nights under any roof, your hosts want you gone, including the ones who love you. They cannot say why, and they feel terrible about it.
Make yourself so useful to one household that they ask you to stay a full season.
You can't say the most important thing. Whatever matters most in any conversation, a warning or an apology or a name, sticks in your throat, and writing it down smears the ink.
Get your most important message across to the one person it was for, without words.
You dream other people's nightmares. Each night you get one from somebody within a mile, complete, with their fears standing in for your own. They sleep soundly that night.
Find the owner of one nightmare and end the thing in their waking life that causes it.
Your shadow resents anyone you grow fond of. It trips them on stairs, tips their drinks and leans the wrong way in lamplight to make them uneasy. It gets bolder the fonder you are.
Leave your shadow behind somewhere, for good, and learn to do without one.
The first solid blow to your head in any fight puts you on the floor for a slow count of ten, whatever your strength or armour. After that you are as tough as you ever were.
Win ten fights in a row in which you were struck first.
Iron and steel that you hold for more than a minute begin to pit and flake. A sword lasts you one fight and a set of tools lasts a week. Bronze, wood and stone are not affected.
Forge a blade yourself, from ore to edge, and carry it unrusted for a year.
You need twice the food and twice the water of anyone your size, and you weaken twice as fast without them. A missed meal feels like a missed day.
Fast for seven days of your own free will, while cooking for other people.
Something on four legs is tracking you. It walks, never runs, and is never more than a week behind. Nothing you carry can kill it. Everyone it has caught before was found dead.
Stop running and face it on ground of your own choosing. If you stand your ground until dawn, it leaves for good.

Somebody in your family line borrowed heavily from people who do not forgive debts, and you are the last name on the contract. Collectors arrive each season, and each visit is less polite than the one before.
Pay it in full, or find the original contract and the flaw in it.
Wherever you stay longer than a month, the weather turns violent: first floods, then gales, then worse. Your neighbours suffer it alongside you, and sooner or later they work out the cause.
Find whatever in the sky has taken offence at you and make your peace with it.

Fate takes an interest in whoever stands closest to you. Your nearest friend at any time is the one the falling beam finds, the fever picks and the stray shot hits. So far it has stopped short of killing them.
Take a blow that was meant for a friend, three times, before it lands on them.
You are being forgotten from the edges inward. Acquaintances go first, then colleagues, then friends. Each month, one more person who knew you looks at you blankly. Family goes last.
Do one thing so plainly yours that a stranger tells the story of it back to you, with your name in it.
You have exactly ten years from the day you bind this, and a pocket watch that counts them down. On the last second you stop like a clock. The watch cannot be lost, sold or broken.
Give some of your remaining time away to someone who needs it more, knowing it will not be returned.

One doorway in three does not lead where it should. You open the pantry and get the cellar, or the cellar of a house down the road. It is never dangerous, never convenient and always a different place.
Walk through a thousand doors without once looking back to check where you came from.
Every sentence you speak has to rhyme with the one before it, or the words will not come out. Short answers are easy. Explaining a plan in a hurry is not.
Win a public argument against someone who is under no such restriction.
Nothing you own stays new. Clothes fray inside a week, tools dull, boots split, and paint flakes off your front door. The wear stops at shabby and never reaches useless.
Own nothing at all for one full year, and get by on what you are lent.
No two clocks agree in your presence, and none of them is right. You are early or late to everything, and people have stopped believing your excuses.
Arrive exactly on time to something that matters more than anything else you have going.
In any group that includes you, small things go wrong for everyone else: spilled ink, lost keys, a broken wagon wheel, a missed tide. People seldom trace it to you.
Lead a company of at least twelve through a hard undertaking with none of them the worse for it.

You have no reflection. Mirrors, water and shop windows show the room behind you and nothing else. After a year, you start to forget what you look like, and portraits of you seem to be of somebody else.
Have your likeness made by someone who loves you, and recognise it.
You can't sleep. You don't die of it and your body carries on, but you are tired from the first week onward and the nights are very long. Drugs, drink and a blow to the head give you an hour at most.
Keep a vigil over someone else's sleep every night for a year.
You hear the passing thoughts of everyone within a hundred paces, all at once, at speaking volume. A village is noisy. A city is a riot. You can't shut it out and you rarely like what you hear.
Find the one mind in the crowd that is calling for help, and answer it.
You fall completely in love with whoever shows you kindness, every time, for exactly one month. Then it is gone as if it never happened. You remember each one clearly, and so do they.
Stay beside one person through thirty-one days and choose them again on the morning after.
Nobody believes anything you say the first time. Warnings, confessions and your own name are all taken as a joke or a lie until you can prove them. The second telling works normally, if you get one.
Be believed at once, by a crowd, when it counts.
Your bones break like a much older person's. A bad fall is a fracture, and a fistfight is three of them. They knit in half the usual time.
Climb a mountain that has killed stronger people and come back down on your own feet.

Anything that hunts picks you out first. In a herd, on a battlefield or on a city street at night, the predator's eye lands on you before anyone else. That goes for wolves, sharks, press gangs and snipers.
Hunt down and face something that hunts people, alone, and come back.
Your wounds will not close on their own. A shaving cut seeps for a day, and a real wound needs fire, stitches and luck. Healing magic works on you at a tenth of its strength.
Give your own blood, freely, to save three lives.

Any weapon you pick up weighs four times what it should, and any armour does the same. You can train up to it, slowly. Tools, pots and walking sticks are spared unless you mean to hit someone with them.
Defeat a trained opponent without lifting a weapon or wearing any protection.

Once a year, on a date you are never told, a stranger arrives who is exactly as skilled as you are and wants you dead. They are a different stranger each time. They do not negotiate and have no life to go back to.
Spare one of them, and still be alive a year later.

A sickness follows a day behind you. Towns you pass through come down with fever a week later and some of the people do not get up again. You never catch it. It can be outrun, but that means never stopping.
Find the cure and carry it back along every road you have travelled.
Every ruler who sees you becomes certain, within the hour, that you are the one who will kill them. They act on it with everything a throne can bring to bear.
Save the life of a ruler who has ordered your death, and let them watch you do it.
War follows you. Any land you settle in is at war inside three years, by invasion, by rebellion or over some border quarrel that nobody can now explain. The fighting starts near wherever you live.
End a war by some means other than winning it.
Each winter in your world lasts a week longer than the one before, starting the year you bind this. In a decade the growing season has lost two months. In three decades there is none.
Find the source of the cold and seal it.

You inherit a throne you never wanted, over a country that is bankrupt and surrounded. Abdication is refused, and every faction at court has a candidate to replace you and is willing to have you killed.
Leave the country stronger than you found it and hand it on to a successor you chose.

Each morning the world has forgotten yesterday's version of you. Whatever you built, promised or earned the day before belongs to nobody, and friends meet you as a stranger. Only what you carry on your person stays yours.
Be remembered across one sunrise by one person, through nothing except what you did for them.
There is another one of you, drawn from the same shelf, who wants your place and is a little better at being you than you are. Your friends have met them, and some like them better.
Meet them face to face and settle which of you keeps your life, by agreement or by a fight.
Your world is being erased from the edges. Far countries go first, turning to white fog on the maps and in people's memories. It advances a mile a day toward wherever you are standing.
Walk into the erased lands, find what is erasing them, and stop it.

Somebody has written a note against your name in the archive's own catalogue: withdrawn, pending review. Scrolls you draw may fail to arrive, and the ones you hold flicker. On some mornings you do too.
Find the clerk who wrote the note and have it struck out before the review is held.
Everyone related to you by blood begins to vanish, the oldest first, one each season. With each of them goes every trace that they lived, except in your own memory. You are last on the list.
Trace your line back to whoever made the bargain that this is the price of, and unmake it.

Whoever is reading your world's story has started to skim. Days are skipped, minor characters blur, and whole towns lose their detail when you aren't looking at them. If the book is closed, that is the end of it.

Say it in person to the one you meant, with everyone who got a letter looking on.

Win a footrace against a faster runner in spite of the fall.

Catch the real thief each time, three times running.
